summary: Sort a singly linked list using insertion sort.
mainInsight: Keep a sorted list built from a dummy head. For each node taken from the input, find its insertion point by scanning the sorted part from the dummy (optionally resetting from the dummy only when needed), splice it in, and continue with the saved next pointer.

approaches.name: Insertion sort
approaches.summary: Insert each node into the sorted prefix.

approaches.name: Merge sort
approaches.summary: Divide at the middle and merge sorted halves.

commonMistakes: Losing the rest of the list by not saving next
Always scanning from the head even for ascending input (still correct)
Returning the dummy instead of dummy.next

promptVariants: Why use a dummy head when building the sorted list?
options: A node may have to be inserted before the current head, and the dummy removes that special case
It stores the length of the sorted list built so far
It reverses the order of the already sorted nodes
It lets you compare each node with the tail in O(1)
cards.answer: A node may have to be inserted before the current head, and the dummy removes that special case
cards.explanation: The dummy's next always points to the smallest node.

incorrectOptionExplanations.It stores the length of the sorted list: The dummy does not store a length.
incorrectOptionExplanations.It lets you compare each node with the t: The tail is not used for insertion.

promptVariants: What must be saved before relinking a node into the sorted list?
cards.answer: The next pointer of the node being inserted: inserting rewires node.next, so without saving it you would lose the rest of the unsorted list.
cards.explanation: Typical bug: infinite loop or truncated list.
Each insertion may scan the whole sorted prefix.

promptVariants: Complete the statement: Space complexity (excluding the input): ___
What does the algorithm return for an empty list or a single node?
options: The input itself (None or the single node): the loop does nothing
An error: there is nothing to sort in the list
A new dummy node that points to None only
None, even when the list holds one single node
cards.answer: The input itself (None or the single node): the loop does nothing
cards.explanation: dummy.next is returned in all cases.

incorrectOptionExplanations.An error: there is nothing to sort in th: The loop simply does not run.
incorrectOptionExplanations.A new dummy node that points to None onl: The dummy's next is returned, which is the input.
incorrectOptionExplanations.None, even when the list holds one singl: A single node is already sorted.
